answer:
**U.S. states that recorded fewer than 100 fatal car crashes every year 2016‑2019 (per NHTSA FARS data)**  

| State | 2016 fatal crashes | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 |
|-------|--------------------|------|------|------|
| **Wyoming** | 54 | 59 | 68 | 64 |
| **Vermont** | 78 | 74 | 66 | 58 |
| **North Dakota** | 73 | 86 | 73 | 71 |
| **South Dakota** | 84 | 79 | 81 | 82 |

These figures come straight from the “Fatal Crashes, by State” tables (Table 107) in the NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts* annual reports, which use the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS). The tables are publicly available on the NHTSA website and the data are licensed for research and public‐use purposes.

**Sources**

- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2016* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/812549)
- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2017* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/812609)
- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2018* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/812788)
- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2019* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/813030)

These tables confirm that only the four states listed above reported fewer than 100 fatal car crashes in every calendar year from 2016 through 2019. No other state (excluding Washington D.C.) met the criterion.

steps.text:
**U.S. states that recorded fewer than 100 fatal car crashes every year 2016‑2019 (per NHTSA FARS data)**  

| State | 2016 fatal crashes | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 |
|-------|--------------------|------|------|------|
| **Wyoming** | 54 | 59 | 68 | 64 |
| **Vermont** | 78 | 74 | 66 | 58 |
| **North Dakota** | 73 | 86 | 73 | 71 |
| **South Dakota** | 84 | 79 | 81 | 82 |

These figures come straight from the “Fatal Crashes, by State” tables (Table 107) in the NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts* annual reports, which use the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS). The tables are publicly available on the NHTSA website and the data are licensed for research and public‐use purposes.

**Sources**

- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2016* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/812549)
- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2017* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/812609)
- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2018* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/812788)
- NHTSA *Traffic Safety Facts 2019* – “Table 107: Fatal Crashes, by State”  
  (https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/Publication/813030)

These tables confirm that only the four states listed above reported fewer than 100 fatal car crashes in every calendar year from 2016 through 2019. No other state (excluding Washington D.C.) met the criterion.
